title: Machine learning prediction of adverse events during minutes 15–30 of recovery in patients event-free at 15 min after sedated gastrointestinal endoscopy
summary: In 1,070 patients undergoing sedated gastrointestinal endoscopy at West China Hospital, XGBoost predicted prespecified respiratory or hemodynamic events during minutes 15–30 of recovery among patients event-free at minute 15. The model achieved an AUC of 0.910 in the independent validation set (cross-validated training AUC 0.971). Prospective, temporally separated evaluation and external validation are still needed.
ai_technology: XGBoost with Boruta feature selection and SHAP interpretation
organization: Department of Anesthesiology, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, China; West China School of Nursing, Sichuan University, Chengdu, China

evidence.tested: The study evaluated six supervised models in a retrospective cohort; 103 of 1,070 patients had the prespecified event. XGBoost had validation AUC 0.910, PR-AUC 0.815 and Brier score 0.076, using five final predictors.
evidence.unknown: The cohort came from one hospital and the study calls for prospective testing with predictor and outcome windows separated in time, plus external validation, before clinical implementation.
evidence.ai_role: Boruta selected candidate predictors; XGBoost estimated risk of the specified post-anesthesia events, and SHAP described contributions without implying causality.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
